mainTopic: Ten טפחים as a separate domain: רבי יוסי's ברייתא, and the source for the כפורת being one טפח
overview: The גמרא wants to show that ten טפחים off the ground is a real boundary, which is why a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים tall. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says the שכינה never came down to earth and משה and אליהו never went up to heaven. Five פסוקים seem to say otherwise. Each time the answer is the same: the שכינה stayed above ten טפחים, and משה and אליהו stayed below ten. Next the גמרא checks the calculation that the ארון (nine טפחים) plus the כפורת (one טפח) equals ten. The ארון's height is written in the תורה, but the כפורת's thickness is not. רבי חנינא teaches that we learn it from the smallest measurement among the vessels, the one-טפח frame (מסגרת) of the שלחן. The גמרא asks why we don't use the larger vessels, the smaller ציץ, or the tiny זר. In the end it rules that we compare only items whose measurements are written in the תורה. רב הונא then offers a different source: the 'face' of the כפורת, since no face is less than a טפח. The גמרא begins to question that proof, and the question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Heaven and earth are separate domains
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי teaches that the שכינה never came down and משה and אליהו never went up, because heaven and earth are two separate realms.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says the שכינה never came down below, and משה and אליהו never went up to heaven. The source is the פסוק: 'The heavens are the heavens of ה׳, and the earth He gave to people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to support the idea that ten טפחים off the ground is a boundary between two separate domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says heaven and earth never truly mix. The rest of this passage will show that the dividing line between them is exactly ten טפחים. That is the support for the rule that a סוכה below ten טפחים does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the background for why ten טפחים is the minimum height of a valid סוכה. Below ten is not considered its own domain.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
The Divine Presence never came down below,
and Moses and Elijah never went up on high,
as it says: "The heavens are the heavens of God,
and the earth He gave to people."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the earlier claim that ten טפחים is a separate domain.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that above ten טפחים is a separate realm.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי, based on Psalms 115:16.

steps.title: Challenge: God came down on Mount Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the שכינה never came down, when the פסוק says ה׳ came down onto הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the שכינה really never come down? But the פסוק says, 'And ה׳ came down onto הר סיני'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first half of רבי יוסי's statement with a פסוק that says the שכינה came down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said the שכינה never came down. The פסוק at מתן תורה clearly says ה׳ 'came down.' That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: And did the Divine Presence never come down below?
But it is written: "And God came down onto Mount Sinai"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first claim of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that the שכינה never came down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly says ה׳ came down onto הר סיני.

steps.title: Answer: The Divine Presence stayed above ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The שכינה came down, but it stayed more than ten טפחים above the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שכינה came down only to a point above ten טפחים and never entered the earthly realm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer redefines what 'below' means. Anything from ten טפחים and up still counts as the heavenly realm. So the שכינה came 'down' without truly entering the earthly domain.

phrases.english: Above ten handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from הר סיני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the boundary: ten טפחים is the dividing line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שכינה came all the way down into the earthly realm.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שכינה stayed above ten טפחים, which is still the heavenly realm.

steps.title: Challenge: His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second פסוק: in the future, 'His feet will stand on הר הזיתים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says, 'And His feet will stand on that day on הר הזיתים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to the idea that the שכינה never comes down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק sounds even stronger, since 'feet standing on' a mountain suggests actual contact with the ground. It seems hard to say this is still above ten טפחים.

phrases.english: But it is written: "And His feet will stand on that day
on the Mount of Olives"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְעָמְדוּ רַגְלָיו בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא עַל הַר הַזֵּיתִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שכינה never came down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes ה׳'s 'feet' standing on a mountain.

steps.title: Answer: Again, above ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the שכינה will stay above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It will be above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer: even in that future scene, the שכינה stays above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule applies here. Even language as strong as 'standing on' a mountain is read as staying within the heavenly zone above ten טפחים.

phrases.english: Above ten handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from הר הזיתים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שכינה remains above ten טפחים.

steps.title: Challenge: Moses went up to God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the second half of the ברייתא: the פסוק says 'משה went up to God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Did משה and אליהו really never go up to heaven? But the פסוק says, 'And משה went up to God'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to challenging the second claim of רבי יוסי, that people never went up to heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the challenges were about the שכינה coming down. Now the question runs the other way: did a human enter the heavenly realm? The פסוק about משה seems to say he did.

phrases.english: And did Moses and Elijah never go up on high?
But it is written: "And Moses went up to God"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עָלוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאֵלִיָּהוּ לַמָּרוֹם? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first claim of the ברייתא to the second.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that משה and אליהו never went up to heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says משה went up to God.

steps.title: Answer: Moses stayed below ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: משה went up, but he stayed below the ten-טפחים line.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was below ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that משה never crossed above ten טפחים, so he stayed in the earthly realm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the earlier answer. The שכינה stays above ten, and humans stay below ten. So both halves of רבי יוסי's statement use the same boundary.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction of the answer. For the שכינה the answer is 'above ten' (לְמַעְלָה), and for משה and אליהו it is 'below ten' (לְמַטָּה). It is the same line seen from opposite sides.

phrases.english: Below ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about משה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the ten-טפחים boundary from below.

steps.title: Challenge: Elijah went up in a whirlwind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק that אליהו went up to heaven in a storm.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says, 'And אליהו went up in a storm to the heavens'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, this time with the famous ascent of אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק explicitly uses the word 'heavens' (השמים). That seems to say אליהו entered the heavenly realm itself.

phrases.english: But it is written: "And Elijah went up in a whirlwind to the heavens"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the claim about people going up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אליהו never went up to heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says he went up 'to the heavens.'

steps.title: Answer: Elijah also stayed below ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Here too, אליהו stayed below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was below ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way: אליהו never passed the ten-טפחים line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the word 'heavens' does not mean he crossed into the heavenly domain. He still stayed below the ten-טפחים boundary.

phrases.english: Below ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about אליהו.

steps.title: Challenge: Moses grasped the throne and was covered by God's cloud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in איוב, explained by רבי תנחום, which says ה׳ spread His radiance and cloud over משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says, 'He grasps the face of the throne; He spreads His cloud over him.' And רבי תנחום said this teaches that ה׳ spread the radiance of His שכינה and His cloud over משה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge: according to רבי תנחום, משה was wrapped in God's own cloud and radiance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes beyond 'going up.' The cloud and the shine of the שכינה were on משה, which suggests he was inside the heavenly realm itself. The word פַּרְשֵׁז is read as a combination of words: פֵּירַשׂ (spread), שַׁדַּי (the Almighty), and זִיו (radiance).

keyTerms.meaning: A word read as פֵּירַשׂ + שַׁדַּי + זִיו, meaning 'the Almighty spread His radiance'

phrases.english: But it is written: "He grasps the face of the throne,
He spreads His cloud over him,"
and Rabbi Tanchum said:
This teaches that the Almighty spread
of the radiance of His Presence and His cloud over him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״מְאַחֵז פְּנֵי כִּסֵּא פַּרְשֵׁז עָלָיו עֲנָנוֹ״, וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the claim that people never went up, now based on a דרשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that משה never entered the heavenly realm.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳'s own radiance and cloud were spread over משה, which suggests he was inside the heavenly domain.

steps.title: Answer: Still below ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Even this happened while משה was below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was below ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cloud and radiance reached משה while he stayed below the ten-טפחים line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The radiance came down to משה. That does not mean משה went up into the heavenly realm. He stayed in his own domain.

phrases.english: Below ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי תנחום's teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה received the cloud while staying below ten טפחים.

steps.title: Challenge: But Moses grasped the throne itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses on: the פסוק still says משה 'grasped the face of the throne,' and the throne is in heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the פסוק says, 'He grasps the face of the throne'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: even if the cloud came down to משה, he still took hold of the heavenly throne.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer explained the cloud, but not the grasping. If משה held the כסא הכבוד, it seems he must have reached the heavenly realm.

phrases.english: In any case, "He grasps the face of the throne" is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the previous answer as incomplete and focuses on the word 'grasps.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that משה stayed below ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grasping the throne means touching something in the heavenly realm.

steps.title: Answer: The throne was lowered to ten, and Moses held it from below
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ lowered the throne down to ten טפחים, and משה took hold of it while staying below.
steps.simpleTranslation: The throne was extended down for him to ten טפחים, and he grabbed onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the throne came down to the ten-טפחים line, so משה could hold it without leaving his realm. This closes the passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The throne came down to the edge, ten טפחים, and stopped there. משה reached it from below. Neither side crossed the boundary, so רבי יוסי's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It was surely extended / lowered down

steps.whatToRemember: In every case, the שכינה stays above ten טפחים and people stay below ten טפחים. So ten טפחים is a real boundary between domains, and this is why a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים tall to count as its own space.
steps.whyThisMatters: This passage is the source for the ten-טפחים boundary that shows up across many הלכות. It explains the minimum height of a סוכה in this סוגיא.

phrases.english: The throne was surely extended down for him
to ten, and he grabbed onto it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתַּרְבּוֹבֵי אִישְׁתַּרְבַּב לֵיהּ כִּסֵּא עַד עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the final challenge and ends the cycle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the event so that the boundary is never crossed: the throne was lowered to the line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה must have entered heaven to grasp the throne.
steps.terutzMaskana: The throne came down to ten טפחים, and משה held it from below, so the boundary stays intact.

steps.title: Where do we know the Ark cover was one handbreadth?
steps.stepSummary: The ארון's nine טפחים are stated in a פסוק, but the תורה never gives the כפורת's height. So how do we know it was one טפח?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the ארון was nine טפחים tall, because the פסוק says it was a cubit and a half high. But how do we know the כפורת was one טפח thick? רבי חנינא taught that for every vessel משה made, the תורה gave its length, width and height. For the כפורת it gave only the length and width, not the height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the claim it relied on earlier: that the ארון plus the כפורת equal exactly ten טפחים. Nine is written in the פסוק, but where does the one טפח come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cubit and a half is nine טפחים, so the ארון's height has a clear source. רבי חנינא's teaching proves the problem is real: the תורה deliberately left out the כפורת's height, so we can't simply look it up. Without a source for one טפח, the whole 'ten טפחים' calculation is shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (this part is fine, but…)
The golden cover placed on top of the ארון
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Here the כפורת's 'height' means its thickness, since it is a flat slab lying on top of the ארון.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that the שכינה never came down below ten טפחים depends on this one טפח. Without it, the ארון and כפורת would only reach nine.

phrases.english: Granted, the Ark was nine [handbreadths],
as it is written: 'And they shall make an Ark of acacia wood;'
two and a half cubits its length,
and a cubit and a half its width,
and a cubit and a half its height.'
But that the Ark cover was a handbreadth, from where do we know?
For Rabbi Chanina taught:
All the vessels that Moshe made,
the Torah gave for them

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּת אׇרְכָּן וּמִדַּת רׇחְבָּן וּמִדַּת קוֹמָתָן.
phrases.english: the measure of their length, width, and height.

phrases.aramaic: כַּפּוֹרֶת, מִדַּת אׇרְכָּהּ וּמִדַּת רׇחְבָּהּ — נָתְנָה,
phrases.english: For the Ark cover, the measure of its length and width it gave;
the measure of its height it did not give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier calculation (ארון 9 + כפורת 1 = 10) and asks for the source of the כפורת's one טפח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the כפורת being one טפח thick, since the תורה doesn't state it.

steps.title: Learn from the smallest measurement among the vessels
steps.stepSummary: We take the smallest measurement given for any vessel, the one-טפח frame of the שלחן, and apply it to the כפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go and learn from the smallest measurement among the vessels. The פסוק says about the שלחן: 'Make for it a frame one טפח all around.' Just as there it is one טפח, so too here it is one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the continuation of רבי חנינא's ברייתא from step 14, which answers the question. Since the כפורת has no stated height, we borrow the smallest measurement found among the משכן vessels, which is one טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The frame (מסגרת) of the שלחן is described as one טפח. The גמרא uses 'מה להלן… אף כאן', meaning 'just as there… so too here', to carry that measurement over to the כפורת. This gives us the missing one טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and learn (draw a lesson from elsewhere)
The smallest measurement among the vessels
The frame or border around the שלחן
Just as there… so too here

phrases.english: Go and learn from the smallest of the vessels,
as it is said: 'And you shall make for it a frame'
of a handbreadth all around,'

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן טֶפַח, אַף כָּאן טֶפַח.
phrases.english: just as there it is a handbreadth, so too here it is a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי חנינא's ברייתא begun in step 14 and so answers the question 'מְנָלַן' raised there.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Derive one טפח from the frame of the שלחן, the smallest measurement among the vessels.

steps.title: Why not learn from the vessels themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: why not learn the כפורת's size from the main bodies of the vessels, which are much bigger?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from the vessels themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Why pick the small frame instead of the full size of the vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels themselves measure at least an אמה. Learning from them would make the כפורת much thicker than one טפח. So there seem to be two possible sources, and the challenge asks why we chose the small one.

phrases.english: But let us derive from the vessels themselves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source chosen in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the one-טפח frame as the source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a larger possible source, the vessels' own size, so why prefer the small frame?

steps.title: Grab too much and you hold nothing
steps.stepSummary: When unsure between a large amount and a small one, we take the small one, because it is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you didn't grab anything. If you grabbed a little, you grabbed something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using a general rule of reasoning: when in doubt, go with the smaller amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smaller measurement is included inside the larger one, so it is definitely correct at least that far. Picking the larger one has no certain basis. That is why we learn from the one-טפח frame and not from the full vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: If you grab a lot, you hold nothing
If you grab a little, you hold it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used throughout ש״ס: when a measurement is in doubt, we assume the smaller one.

phrases.english: If you grasped much, you did not grasp;
if you grasped little, you grasped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might learn from the bigger measurement of the vessels themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: We take the smaller amount, because it is the certain one.

steps.title: Then why not learn from the even smaller ציץ?
steps.stepSummary: If we always choose the smaller amount, the ציץ is only two fingers wide. That is smaller than a טפח, so why not learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from the ציץ! A ברייתא teaches that the ציץ was like a gold plate, two fingers wide, stretching from ear to ear. Two lines were written on it: the name of ה׳ on top, and 'קדש ל' below. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי said: I saw it in Rome, and 'קדש לה׳' was written on one line!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the 'take the smaller' rule against the answer. The ציץ, the gold headplate of the כהן גדול, is smaller still, so why not use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טפח is four fingers, and the ציץ was only two fingers wide. Following 'take the smaller' to its end, the כפורת should be two fingers, not a טפח. The details about the writing are simply part of the ברייתא being quoted. The key point is the width.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead

steps.confusionAlert: The argument about one line or two lines is a side detail. The challenge is only about the ציץ being two fingers wide.

phrases.english: But let us derive from the frontplate, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: צִיץ דּוֹמֶה כְּמִין טַס שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: The frontplate resembles a kind of plate of gold,
and it is two fingerbreadths wide
and extends from ear to ear,
and written on it are two lines:
'Yod Heh' (God's name) above,
and 'Kodesh Lamed' below.
And Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei said:
I saw it in Rome,
and written on it was 'Holy to ה׳' on one line!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 17's 'take the smaller' rule to suggest an even smaller source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The one-טפח derivation from the שלחן's frame.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the smaller amount is always preferred, the two-finger ציץ beats the one-טפח frame.

steps.title: A vessel is learned only from a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ is an ornament the כהן גדול wears, not a vessel. A vessel can only be compared to another vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn a vessel from a vessel. We do not learn a vessel from an ornament.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the ציץ as a source because it is an ornament, not a vessel. This answer is only temporary: the next steps challenge it, and step 25 gives a new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ belongs to the בגדי כהונה (the כהן גדול's garments), not to the כלי המשכן. Since the כפורת is a vessel, it must be compared to another vessel. The smallest vessel measurement is the שלחן's one-טפח frame, so the derivation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / compare (one case to another)
An ornament or piece of jewelry

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the ציץ is excluded because it is an ornament, not a vessel. Keep this reason in mind: it is challenged in steps 20–24 and replaced by a new rule in step 25.

phrases.english: We derive a vessel from a vessel,
and we do not derive a vessel from an ornament.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and confirms the source given in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-finger ציץ might be the smallest source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ is an ornament, so only vessels count, and the one-טפח frame stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the ציץ is excluded as an ornament, so the one-טפח frame of the שלחן remains the source. The reason is revised in step 25.

steps.title: Why not learn from the crown, which can be tiny?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't learn the כפורת's thickness from the זר, which can be any size at all, even smaller than a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from the crown (זר) instead! As the Master said: the crown can be any tiny size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule of taking the smallest measurement. The זר on the vessels can be any size, even tinier than a טפח, so why not use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the ציץ was pushed aside because it is not a vessel. But the זר sits on the vessels themselves, so that reason does not work here. If we always pick the smallest amount, the זר should win.

keyTerms.meaning: Crown: a decorative rim on some of the משכן vessels
As the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)
Any amount at all, even tiny

phrases.english: And let us derive it from the crown.
phrases.notes: The זר was a decorative rim found on the ארון, the שלחן, and the מזבח הזהב.

phrases.english: As the Master said: the crown can be any size!
phrases.notes: The תורה gave no size for the זר, so even a tiny one is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ציץ was rejected for not being a vessel, the גמרא brings a smaller measurement that is attached to a vessel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from Step 17 that we take the smallest measurement, combined with the answer from Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זר belongs to a vessel and has no minimum size. If we always go smaller, the כפורת should be learned from it and could be thinner than a טפח.

steps.title: A vessel is learned from a vessel, not from decoration
steps.stepSummary: We compare a real vessel to another real vessel, not to a decorative finishing piece like the זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn a vessel from a vessel. We do not learn a vessel from the decoration of a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the זר is only an added decoration, not the vessel itself. So it cannot be used to measure the כפורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כפורת is a real, main vessel. The זר is only a finishing touch that makes a vessel look nice. A main item must be compared to another main item, not to its decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / learn (one law from another)
A vessel's finishing or decoration, not the main body

phrases.english: We derive a vessel from a vessel,
but we do not derive a vessel from the finish of a vessel.
phrases.notes: The זר is a 'finish', a decorative addition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the זר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in category: main vessel versus decorative finish.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any small measurement connected to a vessel could be used for the כפורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a measurement of a real vessel counts. Decorations like the זר are excluded.

steps.title: The table's frame is also just a finish
steps.stepSummary: If decorations cannot be used, the מסגרת of the שלחן is also a finish, so how could we learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the frame (מסגרת) is also just the finish of a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new rule against the original answer. The one-טפח measure came from the מסגרת of the שלחן, and that also seems like an added decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 learned the כפורת from the מסגרת. But if decorations do not count, the מסגרת might not count either. Then the whole source for one טפח falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is correct)
The frame or border of the שלחן

phrases.english: If so,
the frame is also the finish of a vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מִסְגֶּרֶת נָמֵי הֶכְשֵׁר כְּלִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 21 to attack the source in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of one טפח from the מסגרת of the שלחן (Step 15).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a finish cannot teach about a vessel, and the מסגרת is a finish, then the מסגרת cannot be the source either.

steps.title: The frame was underneath, holding up the table
steps.stepSummary: The מסגרת was below the tabletop and held it up, so it is a real part of the vessel, not decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its frame was below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מסגרת was under the tabletop, between the legs. Because it held up the table, it is part of the vessel itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece that supports the vessel does real work, so it counts as the vessel. This puts the מסגרת on the 'vessel' side of the line drawn in Step 21, unlike the זר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its frame (the frame of the שלחן)

phrases.english: Its frame was below.
phrases.notes: Below the tabletop, between the legs, holding the table up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the מסגרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the physical position of the מסגרת makes it part of the vessel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מסגרת is a decorative finish like the זר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מסגרת supported the tabletop from below, so it is part of the vessel.

steps.title: What about the view that the frame was on top?
steps.stepSummary: The answer only works for one opinion. According to the view that the מסגרת was above the tabletop, it is only a finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says its frame was below. But for the one who says its frame was above, what can you say? This is the finish of a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that there is a disagreement about where the מסגרת was. For the opinion that it was on top as a rim, the answer from Step 23 does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מסגרת sat on top of the table like a rim, it held nothing up. Then it is only decoration, just like the זר. So the source from the מסגרת fails according to this opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
its frame was below,
but according to the one who says
its frame was above,
what is there to say?
This is the finish of a vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִסְגַּרְתּוֹ לְמַטָּה הָיְתָה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִסְגַּרְתּוֹ לְמַעְלָה הָיְתָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in Step 23 depends on one side of a disagreement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 23 that the מסגרת was below.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that the מסגרת was on top, it supports nothing and is only a finish. By the rule of Step 21, it could not be the source.

steps.title: A new rule: learn from what the תורה measured
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'vessel versus finish' rule. Instead, we learn from items the תורה gave a measurement to, and the ציץ and זר have no measurement in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: we learn something the תורה gave a measurement to from something else the תורה gave a measurement to. The ציץ and the זר cannot prove anything, because the תורה gave them no measurement at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its earlier answer with a better rule that works for everyone. The כפורת and the מסגרת both have measurements in the תורה, but the ציץ and זר do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gave the כפורת a length and width, and gave the מסגרת a size of one טפח. So they belong together. The ציץ and זר got their sizes only from the חכמים, so they are not a fair comparison. This one rule removes both challenges, no matter where the מסגרת was.

keyTerms.meaning: That the תורה gave a measurement to
The gold head-plate of the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason we learn the כפורת from the מסגרת: both have measurements written in the תורה. The ציץ and זר have none, so they are left out.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא means the גמרא is dropping the 'vessel versus finish' answer. It is not adding to it. The new rule also replaces the reason given for the ציץ in Step 19.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁנָּתְנָה בּוֹ תּוֹרָה מִדָּה
phrases.english: Rather: we derive something the Torah gave a measurement to
phrases.notes: The כפורת: the תורה gave its length and width.

phrases.english: from something the Torah gave a measurement to,
phrases.notes: The מסגרת: the תורה says it is one טפח.

phrases.english: and the head-plate and the crown cannot prove otherwise,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה בָּהֶן תּוֹרָה מִדָּה כְּלָל.
phrases.english: since the Torah gave them no measurement at all.
phrases.notes: Their sizes come from the חכמים, not from the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁנָּתְנָה בּוֹ תּוֹרָה מִדָּה מִדָּבָר שֶׁנָּתְנָה בּוֹ תּוֹרָה מִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24 by giving a new rule in place of the 'vessel versus finish' distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the earlier rule with a new principle of comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We compare only by type: vessel versus finish, or vessel versus ornament. That fails for the view that the מסגרת was on top.
steps.terutzMaskana: We compare items whose measurements are written in the תורה. This leaves out the ציץ and זר, and keeps the מסגרת as the source.

steps.title: רב הונא: a face is at least one טפח
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא gives a different source. The פסוק speaks of the 'face' of the כפורת, and a face is never less than a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: we learn it from here: 'On the face of the כפורת, toward the east.' And no face is less than a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a completely different source for the one-טפח thickness of the כפורת. He learns it from a word in a פסוק instead of from another vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יום כפור says the blood was sprinkled 'on the face' of the כפורת. The front edge of the כפורת is called its 'face', and a face is at least a טפח. So the כפורת's thickness, which is its front edge, must be one טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: On the face of the כפורת, toward the east (ויקרא טז:יד)

steps.whyThisMatters: רב הונא's source comes straight from a פסוק. It avoids the whole back-and-forth about the ציץ, the זר, and the מסגרת.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: from here:
"On the face of the Ark cover, toward the east,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יד, the sprinkling of blood on יום כפור.

phrases.english: and there is no face less than a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source in place of the comparison to the מסגרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כפורת is one טפח thick, learned from the word פני in the פסוק, since a face is at least a טפח.

steps.title: Maybe the 'face' means a different kind of face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב הונא: why assume the 'face' of the כפורת is a human face of a טפח? Say it is like the face of something else, which could be smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is like the face of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a question against רב הונא's proof from the word 'face.' This line is a setup, and the end of the sentence, saying which smaller face, comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's proof depends on the claim that a face is never smaller than a טפח. That is true of a human face, but the word 'face' could describe a smaller creature. If so, the proof that the כפורת is at least a טפח thick would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...'. This phrase offers another possible reading to challenge an assumption.
'Like the face of...'. The word אַפֵּי means 'face' in Aramaic.
Face. This is the key word from the פסוק that רב הונא built his proof on.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The גמרא has not yet said which face it means, and it continues right away on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: But say: like the face of...
phrases.notes: The גמרא is starting to push back here; the rest of the comparison comes in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges רב הונא's proof from Step 26 by questioning what kind of 'face' the פסוק means.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the 'face' of the כפורת must be at least a טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A face is at least a טפח only if it is a human face. If the פסוק means a smaller kind of face, the minimum measurement does not follow.
